title: Maps and projections
examples: Why are some places bigger on maps than they really are?
What is the difference between latitude and longitude?
How does the scale on a map help us?

explain.say: Today we will learn about how maps work.
A map projection is a way to flatten the Earth's curved surface onto a flat map.
The Mercator projection keeps shapes looking correct for navigation.
Scale on a map shows the ratio between map distance and real distance.
Latitude lines run across the map parallel to the equator.
Longitude lines run up and down, meeting at the poles.

faq.q: Why does Greenland look so big on some maps?
faq.a: It is due to the way the map projection stretches areas near the poles. The Mercator projection exaggerates the size of land far from the equator.
asks: Why is the area wrong on maps?
What makes polar regions look huge?

faq.q: What is the difference between latitude and longitude?
faq.a: Latitude measures how far north or south you are from the equator. Longitude measures how far east or west you are from the prime meridian.
asks: Which lines are horizontal and which are vertical?
How do I find my position using these lines?

faq.q: What does the scale on a map tell me?
faq.a: The scale tells you how many real-world units fit into a certain distance measured on the map. It helps you estimate actual distances.
asks: Is the scale important for distance?
How do I use the scale bar?

faq.a: No, every map projection distorts something, like area or shape, to fit the curved Earth onto a flat surface. You must know what the map sacrifices.
asks: Can any map be perfectly accurate?
What is the trade-off in map making?

faq.q: What are the key lines on a global map?
faq.a: The key lines are the Equator, the Prime Meridian, and the lines of latitude and longitude. These form a grid system.
asks: Where do the main lines cross?
What are the main reference lines on a map?

facts: Latitude lines are always parallel to the Equator.
Longitude lines run from the North Pole to the South Pole.
The Mercator projection preserves angles and shapes well.
Scale provides the ratio between map distance and ground distance.

quiz.say: If a map shows the area of Greenland as much larger than it really is, which property is being distorted?
quiz.why: The Mercator projection stretches areas near the poles, making them look much bigger than they are.

wrong.1: Shape distortion refers to angles, but the main issue with Greenland's size is its area.
wrong.2: Scale is a ratio; while it is affected, 'Polar Distortion' is the specific term for this size change.
wrong.3: Angle distortion relates to the corners and right angles, not the overall size of the landmass.

quiz.say: If a map scale is one centimeter to fifty kilometers, what is the relationship?

options.show: For every 1 cm on the map, the real distance is 50 kilometers.
options.say: For every 1 cm on the map, the real distance is 50 kilometers.

options.show: The map is 50 times smaller than reality.
options.say: The map is 50 times smaller than reality.

quiz.why: The scale directly tells you the conversion factor between the map measurement and the actual measurement.

wrong.0: The scale bar must provide units for both the map and the real world.
wrong.1: The scale relates the unit of measurement, not the total length.
wrong.3: This confuses the ratio with a simple division of size.

quiz.say: Which pair of lines correctly defines a location on Earth?
quiz.why: You need both a north-south position (latitude) and an east-west position (longitude) to pinpoint any spot.

wrong.0: Latitude only tells you how far north or south you are, like a belt around the Earth.
wrong.1: Longitude only tells you how far east or west you are, like a line running up and down.
wrong.3: These are important lines, but they only give two specific coordinates, not the general system.
